title.en: JANUS Connection Scan — Minimal-Core Null and Operator Discrimination
title.ru: JANUS Connection Scan — нулевая проверка минимального ядра и дискриминация оператора

primary_hidden_node_candidate.name: OPERATOR_DISCRIMINABILITY
primary_hidden_node_candidate.definition: Whether a recurring abstract transition remains distinguishable from a matched null population after removing domain, title, provenance and prior-Connection context.
primary_hidden_node_candidate.core_question: Does the recurring operator carry information beyond what the registry schema itself makes common?

connections.machine_observation: The recurring observation -> gate/constraint -> bounded consequence topology is plausible across multiple source families, but its informativeness depends on whether it exceeds a schema-matched null rate.
connections.pattern_description: A repeated minimal core is only interesting when it is less common in structurally similar unrelated JSON.
alternative_explanations: The registry schema may make this topology common by construction.
Evidence-first records often naturally encode a gate between observation and claim.
connections.falsification_route: Construct a matched null corpus preserving JSON depth, field counts and control-flow vocabulary while destroying semantic relations; compare operator frequency and ranking stability.

connections.machine_observation: The suspected transition operator can be described without relying on domain-specific titles visible in filenames.
connections.pattern_description: If the same transition is recovered after title and domain labels are removed, the connection becomes less dependent on lexical framing.
alternative_explanations: Internal JSON field names may still encode the same abstraction.
The operator may be too general to distinguish real structure from schema regularity.
connections.falsification_route: Blind titles, filenames and domain labels, then re-run extraction using only value-level content and independent feature representations.

connections.machine_observation: The recurring bounded-claim operator does not logically require knowing which project, author, or historical branch produced the record.
connections.pattern_description: A candidate relation that survives provenance removal is less vulnerable to source-family clustering and prior-author expectations.
alternative_explanations: Provenance is sometimes part of the meaning, especially for authority or replication claims.
Removing provenance may discard legitimate independence information rather than merely blind the detector.
connections.falsification_route: Run the same detector with provenance fields hidden and compare relation rankings to the provenance-visible result.

connections.machine_observation: The same abstract control topology can be instantiated in biological, material, embedded-system and safety records.
connections.pattern_description: Recurrence across source families is more informative than recurrence within one research lineage, provided common schema effects are controlled.
alternative_explanations: All records may still share a common authoring convention.
The operator may represent a generic decision template rather than a domain-independent invariant.
connections.falsification_route: Stratify by source family and compare within-family versus cross-family recurrence after title, provenance and prior-scan blinding.

connections.machine_observation: The operator becomes useful only if it is more specific than generic schema transitions such as input -> transform -> output.
connections.pattern_description: A candidate invariant must survive abstraction without becoming so generic that almost every JSON record instantiates it.
alternative_explanations: The proposed operator may collapse to a generic computational schema.
A richer operator representation may be required to retain discriminative information.
connections.falsification_route: Increase operator specificity stepwise and report the null separation at each level; retain only the highest abstraction with measurable discrimination.

next_scan_strategy.name: MATCHED_NULL_OPERATOR_BENCHMARK
next_scan_strategy.target: Determine whether recurrent operators in data are rarer or structurally stronger than expected from matched null JSON.
next_scan_strategy.promotion_rule: No operator is promoted beyond DISCOVERED until it shows discrimination against a matched null and survives source-family and context-blinding controls.

canonical_rule: A machine-discovered connection becomes interesting not when it can be described abstractly, but when the abstract description remains specific, survives blindness, and is measurably rarer or more structured than its matched null.
